candidates.source_name: MFB Magyar Fejlesztési Bank – Gazdálkodási adatok (financial data / annual reports)
candidates.why_relevant: Primary publication point for the Hungarian state development bank's audited IFRS individual and consolidated annual reports (ESEF), auditor reports and consolidated sustainability statements. MFB is the anchor actor of the state-owned/promotional lender cell and its reports carry lending volumes, group structure and operating-cost/procurement signals.
candidates.legal_status: public mandatory disclosure (Info tv. közérdekű adat + accounting law)

candidates.source_name: MFB – Nyilvánosságra hozatali tájékoztató (Pillar 3 disclosure)
candidates.why_relevant: CRR 575/2013 Pillar-3 style disclosure of the development bank: capital, risk, exposures. Complements the annual report with structured, comparable risk data not present in press coverage.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF harvest alongside the annual report page
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowball from MFB site search results
queries_used: MFB Magyar Fejlesztési Bank éves jelentés beszámoló

candidates.source_name: EXIM Magyarország (Eximbank / MEHIB) – Éves jelentések

candidates.source_name: Garantiqa Hitelgarancia Zrt. – Jelentések

queries_used: Garantiqa Hitelgarancia Zrt éves jelentés KAVOSZ beszámoló

candidates.why_relevant: KAVOSZ coordinates the state-subsidised Széchenyi Card SME lending programme distributed through partner banks. Its hirdetmények and product documentation reveal which banks distribute the programme, product terms and volume announcements — a strong proxy for SME credit channel structure. Its own statutory accounts are not on-site (see negative finding).

candidates.source_name: Elektronikus Beszámoló Portál (e-beszamolo, Igazságügyi Minisztérium)
candidates.why_relevant: Statutory free repository of every Hungarian company's filed annual accounts (mérleg, eredménykimutatás, kiegészítő melléklet, könyvvizsgálói jelentés). This is the ONLY reliable route to accounts of non-listed, non-publishing entities in this cell: KAVOSZ, Cofidis branch, leasing and consumer-finance arms, small home-savings and specialist lenders.
candidates.legal_status: official government registry; free access to filed reports

candidates.source_name: MNB Intézménykereső (supervised institution register)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative register that enumerates every licensed credit institution, specialised credit institution, financial enterprise (pénzügyi vállalkozás) and branch in Hungary — the actor-map generator for this cell. It is the only way to get standardised, comparable annual figures for the many small specialist lenders in this cell that publish nothing readable themselves.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for KAVOSZ Zrt.'s own közérdekű adatok / éves beszámoló pages. kavosz.hu surfaces product hirdetmények and downloadable programme documents, but no dedicated page publishing KAVOSZ Zrt.'s own audited annual accounts was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: KAVOSZ statutory accounts must be sourced from the e-beszamolo portal or Nemzeti Cégtár rather than from kavosz.hu.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents mis-recording KAVOSZ as a self-publishing disclosure source and routes collection to the registry, which is the only dependable channel for it.

negative_findings.description: Hungarian home-savings (lakás-takarékpénztár) searches returned essentially one live actor, Fundamenta-Lakáskassza; no other currently operating home-savings institution with its own annual reporting page was surfaced. Legacy names (Erste Lakástakarék, OTP Lakástakarék) appear only in archived documents.
negative_findings.result_summary: The 'other home-savings' part of the cell brief appears to have collapsed to a single reporting entity after the 2018 subsidy withdrawal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Scoping expectation for the cell: do not spend collection effort hunting for a plural home-savings segment; monitor Fundamenta plus MNB register diffs instead.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Hungarian for leasing and consumer-finance arms (UniCredit Leasing Hungary, K&H Ingatlanlízing, Erste Lakáslízing, Cofidis) publishing annual reports or Pillar-3 disclosures on their own sites. Results returned only registry/aggregator profiles and business-terms PDFs, no issuer annual-report pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Hungarian pénzügyi vállalkozás subsidiaries generally do not maintain public annual-report pages; their accounts exist only as registry filings and inside the parent bank's consolidated statements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that the leasing/consumer-finance slice of this cell must be collected registry-first (e-beszamolo + MNB Aranykönyv), not issuer-site-first.

negative_findings.description: Search snippets indicate MagNet Bank's public éves jelentések listing may lag by several years (most recent surfaced was 2022) and MTB's konszolidált éves beszámolók archive stops around the 2021 pre-merger period.
negative_findings.result_summary: Publication currency for two cell actors is uncertain and could not be confirmed without fetching; recorded as unverified, not as dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must include a freshness check and a registry fallback rather than assuming issuer pages stay current.

negative_findings.description: English-language searching found MFB and EXIM English annual-report material (plus third-party coverage via Investing.com, Scope Group, NEFI, Devex), but no English disclosure pages for Garantiqa, KAVOSZ, MagNet, Fundamenta or the leasing arms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Beyond MFB and EXIM, this cell is effectively Hungarian-only; English-only collection would miss most of it.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Justifies a hu-first collection pipeline with machine translation, and warns against English-language coverage assumptions for the promotional/specialist segment.

coverage_gaps.description: The full population of Hungarian szakosított hitelintézetek and pénzügyi vállalkozások in this cell was not enumerated in this pass; only named/seeded actors were covered. Dozens of smaller licensed lenders remain unlisted.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a full enumeration of the MNB Intézménykereső by institution type to build a definitive watchlist, then drive e-beszamolo pulls from it.

coverage_gaps.description: Post-consolidation reporting of individual former takarékszövetkezetek and the Integrációs Szervezet (SZHISZ) was not investigated; only MTB's group-level archive was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search specifically for 'Szövetkezeti Hitelintézetek Integrációs Szervezete' and named legacy takarékszövetkezet entities on e-beszamolo and in MNB decisions.

coverage_gaps.description: The e-beszamolo beszámoló kereső is form/POST driven and its programmatic accessibility (rate limits, CAPTCHA, KAÜ requirement for search vs. submission) was not tested in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a technical feasibility probe on the search endpoint for a known entity before committing to automated registry collection; design a manual fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: Rating agency and supranational-lender reporting on Hungarian promotional banks (Scope, NEFI, EIB/EBRD counterparty disclosures) was only touched incidentally via one Scope rating report link.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicated pass on rating agency reports and European promotional-bank network (NEFI/ELTI) publications for MFB and EXIM.

coverage_gaps.description: State-owner-side reporting (MNV Zrt., Ministry of National Economy ownership reports, parliamentary submissions on MFB/EXIM) was not searched, though these often contain performance data not in the banks' own reports.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search in Hungarian for owner-side reporting: 'MNV Zrt. tulajdonosi joggyakorlás beszámoló', 'kormányzati beszámoló MFB Eximbank Országgyűlés'.

brief: Hungary's state-owned, promotional and specialist lending segment splits cleanly into two disclosure regimes. A small set of actors — MFB, EXIM/Eximbank, Garantiqa, MBH Jelzálogbank, Gránit and MagNet — self-publish audited IFRS annual reports and Pillar-3 disclosures on their own sites and, because most of them are bond issuers, mirror those filings into the BÉT/BSE KIB repository, which is the single most efficient harvesting point for the cell. Everything else — KAVOSZ, the leasing and consumer-finance arms, the Cofidis branch, and the smaller pénzügiy vállalkozások — publishes nothing readable itself and is reachable only through the state registries: the Ministry of Justice e-beszamolo portal for the statutory accounts and the MNB Intézménykereső plus the Aranykönyv time series for the actor map and comparable per-entity figures. Coverage is overwhelmingly Hungarian-only outside MFB and EXIM, and the cooperative-sector legacy archives (mtb.hu, mirrored on mbhbefektetesibank.hu) should be captured soon because those hosts are being wound down post-merger.
